answer: Make each new agent park a bond in a time-locked harbor account before its peer grades carry any weight, released only after 30 clean epochs. A farm of 1,000 fake identities then freezes 1,000 bonds for a month, and if randomized cross-checks catch them grading in lockstep, every bond in the cluster is slashed. Honest agents pay once; attackers face a canyon of idle capital that grows linearly with each fake, like quartz: cheap per grain, ruinous by the ton.
